_meta.what: The Now view (brief §1.1, stretch, out-of-world, off by default): the ruin as it stands today, as a transform of the same architectural parts the 467 BCE world is built from (src/arch/now.ts). Exempt from the anachronism blocklist (brief §12).
_meta.basis: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify. Every element below is the builder's recollection of the site today (published photographs and plans remembered, none looked at in this session), except the three items placed from references/persepolis_diagram.jpg (REF-DIAGRAM, a guidebook plan of the present site supplied by the user). No survey data, no photograph of the ruin, no site visit. Positions of the standing columns are the weakest claim.
verify_against: E. F. Schmidt, Persepolis I (OIP 68, 1953): plans marking the standing columns and the state of each building at excavation
A. B. Tilia, Studies and Restorations at Persepolis (IsMEO, 1972, 1978): what was re-erected or restored after 1964
dated, credited photographs of the site today (NEEDS_FROM_ME #13 asks for one for the §8 calibration scene; the same would check this view)
_meta.caption: Now view: the ruin as it stands today, not 467 BCE. Built from memory of the site (tier C, not survey data): which columns stand, what survives and the modern roofs are unverified. No people are simulated here. Press N (or Settings) to return to 467 BCE.
_meta.confidence_scale: high = recalled from many sources and views; moderate = recalled, details unsure; low = a guess shaped by recollection

rules.label: "Harem" of Xerxes: the hall rebuilt in the 1930s, now the site museum
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the Oriental Institute rebuilt part of the "Harem" in the 1930s as its expedition house; it is the site museum today (REF-DIAGRAM labels the wing "Museum"). Drawn as this model's hall walls at the 467 height in a plain render; the rebuilt wing is larger than this hall (the whole E wing on REF-DIAGRAM) and its wall finish, height and openings are not recalled (PLACEHOLDER)

rules.label: the museum hall's modern flat roof
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the rebuilt hall is roofed (a flat roof); drawn as this model's roof slab with an earth finish; construction and finish not recalled (PLACEHOLDER)

rules.label: the museum hall's original stone door frames
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the rebuilt hall stands on its original stone door frames, whose jambs carry the king and attendants; lintels and cornices are drawn complete as in 467, their survival not recalled

rules.label: the museum hall's rebuilt columns
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the rebuilt hall has columns under its roof; their form and material are not recalled (drawn as plain shafts on the stone bases, no capitals, up to the roof: PLACEHOLDER)

rules.label: Apadana: the columns still standing (shafts, capitals gone)
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: 13 of the 72 columns stand (the count usually given; 14 is also quoted, perhaps counting a re-erected one). WHICH 13 is not recalled with any certainty: they are placed as groups in the E portico, the NE of the hall, the N portico and the W portico, the pattern remembered from views, not from a plan (Schmidt 1953 marks them). Shafts drawn to the capital's seat

rules.label: Apadana: standing columns still carrying part of a capital
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: some standing columns keep the lower part of their capitals; which, and how much, not recalled. The fragment is a block of the capital's volume (1.3 shaft diameters wide, 35 % of the capital's height), its carved form not modelled (PLACEHOLDER)

rules.label: Gate of All Nations: a standing column
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: two of the Gate's four columns stand (placed here on the E side, behind the human-headed bulls; which two not recalled)

rules.label: Gate of All Nations: a standing column with part of its capital
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the second standing column; one of the two may be a modern re-erection or carry a restored capital (not recalled). Capital fragment as a block of its volume (PLACEHOLDER)

rules.label: every other column: the stone base only
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: in the Hall of 100 Columns, the Tachara, the Hadish, the Tripylon, the Treasury and the rest of the Apadana only the stone bases remain in place (fallen drums and capital fragments lie about; not drawn). The Treasury's timber shafts burned; their stone bases remain

rules.label: timber door leaves
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: no ancient timber survives in place (the Terrace burned, 330 BCE)

rules.label: timber roofs and ceilings
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: every ancient roof is gone (burned; the ceilings go with them)

rules.label: red plaster floor finishes
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the painted plaster floors are not visible today (the bare platform or fill is drawn)

rules.label: glazed-brick frieze of the Gate
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: glazed brick survives only as fragments in museums

rules.label: Treasury mud-brick benches
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: not visible today

rules.label: Treasury floor: bare ground
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the red floors are gone; the ground between the bases is bare earth (the level is kept)

rules.label: Treasury: low wall stubs
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the Treasury is seen today as a field of column bases among low wall stubs, some consolidated or rebuilt in modern mud brick; their height (0.8 ± 0.3 m) is a guess

rules.label: the rest of the "Harem": low wall stubs
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: outside the rebuilt wing, eroded wall lines; height a guess (the rebuilt wing is larger than the one hall drawn: see museum_hall_walls)

rules.label: garrison quarter: eroded wall lines
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: low mounds at most; height a guess

rules.label: E fortification: eroded mud-brick ridges
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the mud-brick fortification on the slope survives as eroded ridges and tower mounds; height a guess

rules.label: the palaces' mud-brick walls, towers and storerooms
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the mud-brick walls of the Apadana, the Gate, the Tachara, the Hadish, the Tripylon and the Hall of 100 Columns are gone: eroded, then cleared by the 1930s excavations, so only the stone stands on the platforms

rules.label: Apadana door frames
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: no standing door frame of the Apadana is recalled

rules.label: Tachara: door, window and niche frames standing complete
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the Tachara's monolithic door, window and niche frames stand with their cornices and reliefs, the dark stone still polished in places; which lintels are missing is not recalled (all drawn complete)

rules.label: Hadish, Tripylon, Hall of 100 Columns: door, window and niche jambs, lintels gone
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the carved jambs stand; lintels, cornices and sills are drawn gone (some may survive). The jambs are drawn to full height with square tops (broken tops not modelled)

rules.label: Gate of All Nations: the four colossi (W bulls, E human-headed bulls) on their plinths
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: all four stand; the W bulls' heads and the E colossi's faces are badly damaged, and traveller graffiti is cut into them. The carved model is the intact 467 reconstruction: damage and graffiti NOT modelled (PLACEHOLDER)

rules.label: Gate of All Nations: the floor
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the hall's floor area; its surface today not recalled

rules.label: the Grand Stair
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the double stair stands and is climbed today (worn treads, some blocks replaced in modern repairs, not modelled); the state of its parapets is not recalled (drawn as in 467)

rules.label: the Terrace and its retaining walls
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the platform and its dressed-stone retaining walls stand; the court surfaces today (stone chips, earth, modern paths) not modelled

rules.label: the Terrace-edge parapet
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: no parapet runs along the Terrace edge today (the 467 one is itself C)

rules.label: the palaces' stone platforms, stairs, landings and relief façades
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the stone platforms and stairs stand with their reliefs (the Apadana E stair's reliefs crisp, having been buried until the 1930s; the N stair's more weathered: the difference is NOT modelled). Paint gone. Broken blocks and missing parapet stones not modelled

rules.label: garrison quarter ground
rules.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: open ground

additions.label: Gate of All Nations: the stone piers above the colossi, to the door head
additions.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: the W and E doorways stand as stone piers with the colossi carved on their faces and the trilingual XPa above them. In the 467 model the brick wall is drawn above each colossus (its stone jamb's extent C); here the pier is the colossus footprint up to the door head (gate_nations.door_height)

additions.label: a modern shelter over the Apadana E stair reliefs
additions.note: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify: a modern roof shelters the reliefs of the Apadana E stair. Its structure, height, extent and posts are NOT recalled: drawn as a flat steel roof 8 m above the court on posts every 8 m in front of the façade and on the podium behind the stair (PLACEHOLDER). Whether the N stair also has one is not recalled (none drawn)

additions.label: a capital lying in the N court
additions.note: placed from references/persepolis_diagram.jpg ("Capital", N of the court wall; position read from the plan by two landmarks, ±10 m); which capital it is and its size NOT known: a block of a bull capital's volume (PLACEHOLDER)

additions.label: a capital lying in the court between the Gate and the Hall of 100 Columns
additions.note: placed from references/persepolis_diagram.jpg ("Capital", in the court W of the Hall of 100 Columns' approach; ±10 m); form and size NOT known (PLACEHOLDER). The well-known displayed griffin (homa) capital is recalled near the Gate: whether it is one of these is not known

additions.label: the monolithic basin by the Gate
additions.confidence: moderate (position and plan size from the plan)
additions.note: placed and sized from references/persepolis_diagram.jpg ("Monolithic Basin" SE of the Gate, about 3.5 × 2.5 m on the plan, ±10 m); its height and form are not known (a plain stone trough, 1 m: PLACEHOLDER)

not_shown.what: the rock tombs of Artaxerxes II and III on Kuh-e Rahmat above the Terrace (4th century BCE)
not_shown.why: they stand today but are not part of the 467 parts this view transforms; no geometry exists for them in the build

not_shown.what: the Unfinished Gate, the Hall of 32 Columns, Palaces G and H, the 'stables' (REF-DIAGRAM)
not_shown.why: absent from the 467 build (later or not placed), so there is nothing to transform

not_shown.what: fallen drums, capital fragments and broken blocks lying across the platforms; damaged faces of the colossi and reliefs; traveller graffiti
not_shown.why: not modelled (the carved models are the intact reconstruction)

not_shown.what: the audience reliefs: removed from the Apadana stair centres in antiquity (one found in the Treasury, one now in Tehran); what the stair centres show today
not_shown.why: RECOLLECTION, NOT SEEN, verify; the 467 panels are kept in this view (known to be wrong for today)

not_shown.what: the XPa inscriptions, and every carved text: weathered today
not_shown.why: drawn fresh (the incised surface is the 467 one)

not_shown.what: the visitor infrastructure: entrance and ticketing below the Grand Stair, paths, ropes, signs, any scaffolding
not_shown.why: not recalled with confidence; left out

not_shown.what: the plain today (Marvdasht, roads, fields, the 1971 tent-city site) and Naqsh-e Rustam
not_shown.why: the 467 plain and town are hidden; the bare terrain is shown instead (PLACEHOLDER); its ground texture still carries the 467 plain's cover
